Invikafusp alfa, a first-in-class dual T cell agonist, showed an objective response in various types of cancer, particularly among patients who did not respond to previous checkpoint inhibitor therapy.
Phase 2 results for Marengo Therapeutics’ first-in-class cancer-targeted bispecific antibody invikafusp alfa showed objective responses across eight tumor types, particularly among patients who had been unresponsive to other immunotherapies.
The results, which stem from a first-in-human Phase 1/2 study called Start-001 were announced Friday at the European Society for Medical Oncology conference in Madrid, showing tumor shrinkage in 56% of patients with various tumor types. These included breast, colorectal, endometrial, gastrosophageal junction, gastric, head and neck, non-small cell lung and bladder cancers, according to a company release. The study showed an 18% objective response rate and a 60% disease control rate across all patients.
Invikafusp alfa, a selective T cell agonist, activates and expands a naturally occurring group of T cells called Vβ, increasing the immune capacity for an antitumor response, Marengo CEO Zhen Su told BioSpace in an email.
“We are pioneering this biology to extend the reach of immunotherapy beyond immune checkpoint blockade, including for patients whose cancers have progressed despite these transformative treatments,” Su said, noting the “remarkable success of Keytruda” as well as the mega-blockbuster’s shortcomings, with certain patients forming a resistance to Merck’s drug over time.
The 62 patients in the study came in with heavily pretreated tumors that showed a high mutational burden. Patients who had previously received an immune checkpoint blockade drug fared better than those who had never been treated with immunotherapy, showing a 20% objective response rate versus 14%, as well as a 68% disease control rate versus 43%.

In terms of safety, the drug demonstrated manageable tolerability typically seen alongside T cell activation, with some low-grade cytokine release and no neurotoxicity.
The study was a proof of concept that activation of Vβ T cells can expand the immune response beyond what PD-1 checkpoint inhibitors like Keytruda can accomplish.
“We believe the key is the different mechanism,” Su said. “Immune checkpoint blockade releases the brakes on existing T cells, but that may not be enough when responsive T cells are too few or dysfunctional.”
Studies have shown that only 20% to 30% of cancers respond to immune checkpoint blockade drugs, with some types even more resistant than others. Marengo has shown that invikafusp alfa’s bispecific approach is effective across tumor types, including both “cold” cancers like colorectal and “hot” ones like non-small cell lung cancer, Su said.
The tissue-agnostic behavior of invikafusp alfa comes from shared immune biology of Vβ-defined T cells that are “part of the normal human immune repertoire,” Su said. He added that “Keytruda’s recent full FDA approval in TMB-high solid tumors reinforces the principle of treating cancers according to shared biology rather than organ of origin.”
Targeting cancer this way fuels what could be the next wave of innovation in oncology, Su said.
“We see the next wave as precision immunology, enabled by next-generation multispecific technologies that select which immune cell subsets to activate and coordinate the signals they receive,” Su said.
Marengo has two FDA fast track designations for invikafusp alfa and plans to take the candidate into late-stage development in 2027, Su said. Meanwhile, the Start-001 trial carries on, with a monotherapy cohort expected to read out in the second half of next year.
The company has also combined invikafusp alfa with Gilead Sciences’ breast cancer antibody-drug conjugate (ADC) Trodelvy in patients with metastatic triple-negative and HR-positive, HER2-negative forms of the disease. Early results from a Phase 2 study called Start-002 showed complete responses in heavily pretreated patients, Su said.
“Our vision is to establish invikafusp alfa as a precision immunotherapy backbone, bringing fresh T-cell responses together with the tumor-killing activity of standard treatments,” Su said. “These findings support a new dimension in immunotherapy that activates and expands fresh, diverse T-cell responses against cancer.”

Red Chris mine. Credit: Newmont
Posted By: Henry Lazenby October 23, 2026
Newmont (NYSE, ASX: NEM) put a price of up to $4.8 billion (C$6.4 billion) on taking its Red Chris copper-gold mine underground in British Columbia, with commercial production targeted for 2033.
The project, about 1,030 km northwest of Vancouver, would produce an annual average of 275,000–325,000 oz. gold and 65,000–85,000 tonnes copper from 2035 through 2040, the company said Thursday in its quarterly results . Newmont owns 70% of Red Chris and operates it alongside Imperial Metals (TSX: III), which holds the balance.
“The cave is now larger and it’s also orientated to prevent any intersection with major fault lines,” President and CEO Natascha Viljoen said on Thursday’s third-quarter analyst call, noting that engineering is at least 60% complete.
The update sets out the funding needed for a major Canadian copper expansion backed by Ottawa . The $4.2-billion to $4.8-billion estimate includes contingency but excludes the cost of transitioning from open-pit to underground mining. It also assumes a C$500-million federal contribution, whose terms have yet to be finalized.
It puts development spending well above the US$2.1 billion estimated in Newcrest’s 2021 prefeasibility study, although the scope has changed: that plan covered three mining blocks over 31 years, while Newmont’s initial stage covers two blocks over 13 years.
Newmont beat Scotiabank’s earnings forecast and outlined lower capital spending for 2027 than the bank expected, analyst Tanya Jakusconek said in a Thursday note. But “these estimates may be overshadowed by the higher capex” at Red Chris, she wrote.
Even so, changes to the project’s scope make direct comparisons with Newcrest’s earlier study unhelpful, Jakusconek said. Red Chris represents about 2% of Scotiabank’s estimate of Newmont’s net asset value.
Shares in Newmont fell 2% to $111.81 on Friday morning in New York, valuing the company at $116.1 billion. The stock has traded in a 12-month range of $76.04 to $135.29.
Construction decision
The feasibility study is nearing completion, with an investment decision expected early next year, Viljoen said. B.C. granted key permits in June through a consent-based process with the Tahltan Nation. Construction could begin in 2027, subject to board approvals.
Ottawa referred the Red Chris expansion to its Major Projects Office in September last year, placing it among the first five selected for help coordinating regulatory approvals and financing.
The initial stage is to produce 3 million oz. gold and more than 850,000 tonnes copper. Newmont sees potential for a mine life of up to 70 years through further development, including East Ridge, but those additions aren’t included in the initial plan. The company expects to fund construction from internal cash flow.
Australian progress
Down Under, Newmont brought forward commercial production at Tanami Expansion 2 in the Northern Territory to the end of June next year from the second half of 2027. Shaft construction is complete, mechanical completion is expected by year-end and commissioning should begin early next year.
The $1.7-billion to $1.8-billion expansion adds a 1,460-metre hoisting shaft and supporting infrastructure to improve underground productivity and extend Tanami’s life beyond 2040.
At Cadia in New South Wales, gold output recovered to 61,000 oz. from 34,000 oz. in the second quarter following April’s seismic disruption . Newmont completed the final blasting step needed to develop Panel Cave 2-3 in September and expects to hand the project over to operations by year-end.
Cave-establishment work at Panel Cave 1-2 has resumed after regulatory approvals following the earthquake. That project remains on schedule.
Water risk
Lihir in Papua New Guinea faces a less certain fourth quarter. Newmont expects higher grades and throughput after completing September maintenance but warned that El Niño conditions affecting water supply could intensify through year-end and hurt production and costs.
Water shortages haven’t yet affected operations, Viljoen said. If conditions worsen, Newmont will prioritize community supplies while continuing mining and stockpiling ore and could bring forward maintenance scheduled for next year.
The company maintained its annual production outlook for the operation. It continues to advance Lihir’s Nearshore Barrier project, due for completion in 2028, to unlock access to additional ore and extend the operation’s life beyond 2040.
At Mexico’s Peñasquito, fourth-quarter silver output is expected to fall to about half the third-quarter level as planned lower grades and throughput reduce production. Peñasquito’s silver output is expected to fall roughly 30% next year because of planned mine sequencing, chief financial officer Brian Tabolt said on the analyst call. The decline would reduce the revenue credits that offset Newmont’s reported gold costs.
Brucejack in B.C. increased quarterly gold production to 72,000 oz. from 53,000 oz., helped by improved access to mining areas and fewer underground bottlenecks. Cerro Negro in Argentina lifted output to 55,000 oz. from 49,000 oz. as mining rates and grades improved.
Growth returns
Across the portfolio, Newmont expects gold production to grow by a low-to-mid single-digit percentage next year, supported by Tanami’s expansion, higher grades at Lihir and Boddington, and extended mining at Yanacocha in Peru.
Development spending is expected to rise by about $500 million next year from this year’s $1.4-billion budget as investment increases at Red Chris and Lihir. Red Chris accounts for half that increase, or about $250 million, Viljoen said, subject to project approval. About $200 million of the overall increase would be offset by lower reclamation spending as Yanacocha’s water-treatment plants near completion.
Unit costs are expected to rise next year because of inflation, diesel prices, currency movements and lower by-product credits. For this year, however, Newmont cut its gold all-in sustaining cost forecast, after by-product credits, to $1,520 per oz. from $1,680, while maintaining production guidance of about 5.3 million ounces.
Third-quarter gold production was essentially unchanged from the previous quarter at 1.3 million ounces. Adjusted earnings rose 23% to $2.3 billion, or $2.20 a share, from $1.9 billion, or $1.71 a share, a year earlier. Free cash flow totalled $1.9 billion.
Newmont ended September with $8.8 billion in cash, before a planned $1.95-billion payment to Barrick Mining (TSX: ABX; NYSE: B) this quarter under their amended Nevada Gold Mines agreement . The August deal provides for adding Barrick’s Fourmile and Newmont’s Fiberline and Mike properties to the joint venture.
BMO Capital Markets analyst Matthew Murphy put Newmont’s $1.9-billion quarterly free cash flow above his $1.4-billion forecast. The company’s preliminary 2027 production outlook implies 5.4 million to 5.5 million oz., below BMO’s previous 5.7-million-oz. estimate, he said in a Thursday note. He is watching for a path back to annual gold production of 6 million ounces.
“Overall, we feel NEM continues to track well versus expectations,” Murphy wrote.

…including 4.5kW motor, bigger 1.4kWh battery and 45mph top speed
Yozma may not have invented the mini moto space, but they certainly helped mainstream it. Together with Tuttios and Sur Rons, Yozma’s IN10 was one of the most popular mini motos out there, and if you surveyed the average group of 14-15-year-olds in a suburban rideout, you’d be hard-pressed not to find at least a few Yozma IN10s among them…
Today Yozma is shipping the IN 11 , which attempts to bridge the gap between entry-level mini-bikes and high-end off-roaders, but at what cost?
Taken in a vacuum, the Yozma IN11 is an impressive update to the IN 10 and actually is more closely specced to the bigger IN10 Pro .
Advertisement - scroll for more content
Yozma IN 11 spec sheet:
4,800W: Peak motor output, up sharply from the prior IN 10’s 2,600W baseline.
200 Nm: Claimed peak torque, delivering aggressive low-end climb performance.
45 mph: Advertised top speed in Race mode. Real world only slightly lower
52V 27Ah = 1404Wh: Removable lithium battery pack, promising up to 55 miles of range in Eco mode with a 5- to 6-hour recharge time. No one has time to drive for 55 miles in Eco Mode. Expect 20-30 miles when gunning it.
~$1,299: Pre-order and promotional launch pricing. Yozma has the swag to demand a higher price point than the sub-$1,000 off-brand offerings, but it isn’t a slam-dunk decision.
Auto Wheelie Assist: Embedded in “Stunt Mode,” this feature allows riders to cap front-wheel elevation between 15° and 40° with anti-tip protection, functioning like digital training wheels for lofting the bike. Wheelies also increase the likelihood of injuries obviously
One-button reverse gear – helps riders maneuver tight trails and tight garage spaces without manhandling the frame.
Brake Light / Magnetic kill switch – nice safety features and substitute for key in some cases.
Tiered riding modes: Four maps (Eco, Sport, Race, Stunt) let users toggle between commuter battery conservation and full-torque delivery.
But we of course, don’t live in a vacuum, and others, including the Heybike Villain and the Engwe Eagle have already brought 52V, 4.5kW motors to the pit bike form factor, sometimes at much lower cost.
I should say here that parents who want to keep their kids’ e-motos in the 20-30mph range are going to be a whole lot happier with the 2.6kW than 4.5kW motors. Two nice safety improvements over the original Yozma IN10 include the magnetic kill switch and brake lights on the IN11.
Electrek’s take: Yozma’s advantages
If we are keeping it real here, there are dozens of similar-sized and spec’d mini-e-motos out there, often at a much lower cost than the Yozma IN11. But I’d argue that as the biggest and most trusted of these brands, Yozma is a safer bet.
Also, the IN11 is just a lot more solid than the random Amazon/Alibaba electric pit bike. Putting the IN11 together is quicker and easier than any other emoto I’ve built, and it just feels a lot more solid.
That feeling extends to the safety features. The brakes are more dialed in. The turning feels a lot tighter, and the overall ride is quieter and lighter. I believe, and my limited testing bears this out, that spec for spec, I got a lot more range on the IN11 than I got on other bikes with similar battery and motor specs. That 200nm of torque feels like it belongs on a much more expensive e-moto.
The wheelie mode is a nice trick (15, 25, or 40 degrees wheelie settings) and something we’ve only seen on Anylands for this price point so far. It is more developed on the IN11 but expect to see this on just about every new pit bike coming out over the next few years.
That said, the price, which is currently fluctuating between $1299 and $1499 (don’t forget your $60 off Electrek code), Yozma is going to be on the more expensive side of the 4.5kW emotos out there and some of the newcomers are bringing an intense value competition to the place where Yozma once dominated by itself.

It’s been a little over two years since Mercedes-Maybach launched its sportiest car ever, the SL 680 Monogram Series , but despite its name, the 680 part of it, anyway, it does not get the S 680 Sedan’s V12 engine.
The luxury four-door, which is the Mercedes-Maybach S 680, has a 6.0-liter V12 handcrafted mill with twin turbos that produces 621 hp (463 kW/630 ps) and 664 lb-ft (900 Nm) of torque. The lesser S 580 model has a 495 hp (370 kW/503 ps) and 516 lb-ft (700 Nm) of torque 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8, taking 4.7 to hit 60 mph (97 kph), 0.4 seconds slower than the S 680.
As for the Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series , it completes the sprint in roughly four seconds, and features the same engine as the Mercedes-Maybach SL 63. This means a 4.0-liter twin-turbo V8, with 577 hp (430 kW/585 ps) and 590 lb-ft (800 Nm) of torque. The peak output is available between 5,500 and 6,500 rpm, and the maximum thrust from 2,500 to 5,000 rpm. The top speed of this model is 161 mph (259 kph).
A used Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series usually goes between $190,000 to $245,000 in today’s used car market Stateside, and if you want a new one, then you will have to prepare at least $225,900, before destination, dealer fees, and options. The pictured car set its owner back $227,550 a couple of months ago, as he bought it new in August 2026. Fast forward to present day, and the man wants it gone for an unknown reason.
The luxury roadster in question has only 240 miles (385 km) on the clock, and due to the low mileage, it hasn’t required servicing yet. As you can expect from such a thing, there are no known flaws yet, because you are looking at a brand new car, offered with a clean Carfax report, and a clean California title.
Photo: Cars&Bids Located in Malibu, this Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series features a Manufaktur Garnet Red exterior paint finish, and a Manufaktur Crystal White interior. It sports a power-operated soft top, Nappa high-end leather upholstery, a Burmester premium sound system, power-adjustable seats with heating and ventilation, the Airscarf neck-warming system, Active Ride Control suspension, 21-inch Maybach alloys, and a few other things.
Other highlights include the dual-zone automatic climate control system, heated steering wheel, a 64-color LED ambient lighting system, illuminated door sills, remote engine start via the Mercedes-Benz app, Maybach logo projectors, topstitched dashboard, door cards, and console trim, illuminated entry system, garage door opener, a rear shelf with a kaleidoscope design, power folding side mirrors, keyless-go, hands-free access, an electronic-operated trunk lid, and many other features.
The third-generation MBUX system is also on deck, and the car sports the adjustable 11.9-inch touchscreen infotainment, a 12.3-inch digital instrument cluster, biometric authentication, voice control, augmented video for navigation, route-based speed adaptation, head-up display, wireless smartphone integration, a wireless charging pad, several USB-C ports, etc.
Mercedes-Maybach’s SL 680 Monogram Series also supports over-the-air updates, and comes with plenty of safety gizmos, including active brake assist, car-to-x communication, active blind spot assist, exit warning assist, surround view system, attention assist, active parking assist, active steering assist, evasive steering assist, active emergency stop assist, traffic sign assist, adaptive braking, and guard 360 security system, among others.
Photo: Cars&Bids The company’s official website also reveals that the luxury roadster comes with a nose-lift system, dynamic engine mounts, high-performance composite brakes, active rear-wheel steering, electromechanical power steering, and an electronic limited-slip rear differential.
Thus, it is not only a more high-end version of the Mercedes-AMG SL 63 , but a significantly reengineered one, with a clear focus on luxury drives. And unlike the regular AMG versions of the new-generation SL, which is currently getting a mid-cycle refresh, in case you forgot, the Maybach model offers seating for two, whereas the AMGs are 2+2 models.
So, how much does the pictured Mercedes-Maybach SL 680 Monogram Series cost? Well, it doesn’t have a sticker price attached to it, because this machine is advertised as part of an ongoing online auction. The vehicle is listed on Cars&Bids, where the gavel will hit the table six days from now. The auction will end next Thursday, on October 29, 2026, and the highest bid at the time of writing was $100,000, which isn’t even half the value of this thing, given that it left the dealership a couple of months ago for over a quarter of a million bucks.
There is obviously a reserve on it, and at $100K, it clearly hasn’t been met, and we are truly curious to find out how much this ride will fetch once the ongoing online auction ends. Ow much is this thing worth in your opinion? Those who want to bid on it, can do so here , on the quoted website, and that’s also where they can check out this Maybach SL in more detail.

By Alison Koo
23 October 2026
The container shipping orderbook has swelled to 46.5% of the active fleet, a post-2009 peak, as carriers race to secure ultra-large tonnage.
With the orderbook at 16.2m teu, newbuilding activity shows no sign of slowing – Chinese shipyards alone have booked a record 4.94m teu this year, accounting for 88% of the total capacity ordered, according to Linerlytica.
The orderbook-to-fleet ratio is also expected to grow, with Maersk and CMA CGM in the market for more giant ships.
Tellingly, Hengli Heavy Industries announced today it had won orders for 52 ultra-large dual-fuel containerships: 20 of 24,000 teu; 20 ; of 19,000 teu; and a dozen of 22,000 teu.
The 24,000 teu orders are believed to be from MSC, which reportedly wants 10 LNG dual-fuelled vessels, while upgrading 10 existing 22,000 teu orders to 24,000 teu. The Swiss-Italian liner major is said to be splashing out close to $2.5bn.

Volvo Cutting 2,500 Additional Jobs Worldwide After Quarterly Revenue Fell 23% YoY
22 photos
Photo: Volvo
Volvo is cutting another 2,500 positions globally, consultants included. The Swedish automaker further relies on natural attrition and targeted exit packages to reach its target. Such a reduction is especially curious when you remember that Volvo still has plenty of new models to bring to market by 2030.
The majority of said reductions will fall in Sweden, with Volvo estimating 2,000 cuts in the automaker's home market. Add the new 2,500 target to the 3,000 positions announced earlier this year, and you get a whopping 5,500 layoffs. Make not mistake about it, Volvo is getting smaller because the current business isn't generating enough money.
Based on the Q3 2026 numbers, the situation is ugly. Revenue fell a whopping 23 percent year over year, with Volvo confirming SEK 66.9 billion as opposed to 86.4 a year ago. That's USD 6.73 billion versus 8.69 a year ago. Given the aforementioned, operating income swung from a profit to a loss.
Even if you exclude joint ventures, associates, and items affecting comparability, an operating loss of SEK 3.7 billion is not the same as the SEK 5.8 billion profit from a year ago. Its adjusted operating margin understandably contracted as well, falling from 6.7 to -5.6 percent.
Wanna talk cash? Okay! Per the attached Q3 2026 report, Volvo burned through SEK 8.9 billion in free cash flow during the quarter, which is more than twice the outflow from the same period last year. Polestar's Q2 2026 losses, unfavorable raw material costs, and a negative revaluation of US emission credits also hurt Volvo, and that's only part of the problem.
Photo: Volvo China is a tremendous headache for the company right now. Volvo reported that its revenue fell there nearly 50 percent year over year, citing intensified price competition and increasingly better Chinese alternatives. By protecting margins rather than chasing sales by matching every rival's discount, Volvo is losing precious market share in this incredibly lucrative market.
A different squeeze came from the United States, where tariffs and the removal of consumer-facing incentives for electrified vehicles have definitely hurt profitability. Changes to legislation triggered the negative CAFE emission credit revaluation. Over in Europe, increasing demand for electric and electrified vehicles offered Volvo something to smile about.
Despite said 5,500 layoffs, Volvo intends to launch all 13 models planned by the end of 2030. The mix is regionally tailored, with certain models developed specifically for Europe, the US, or China. Three of them are due in 2027, specifically two designed for China and one for Europe.
As for the EX60, which is currently hindered by manufacturing issues, the full-electric model has already secured 50,000 orders in Europe. Looking at the bigger picture, Volvo is going after more than office overhead. In addition to cutting positions worldwide, it's also tightening R&D and production costs.
Regarding the latter, Volvo Cars' production will be concentrated around five dedicated plants. Multi-brand assembly with Geely is under consideration for the Ghent and Chengdu plants, and sharing more suppliers and parts with Geely should further reduce costs across the Swedish brand's model range.

Harley-Davidson El Sicario Is the Bad Boy of the Chicano Kin
46 photos
Photo: Thunderbike
In all the ways that matter, the term sicario doesn't really mean anything good. Which kind of raises the question why someone would choose it to describe a Chicano-style custom motorcycle based on the Harley-Davidson Heritage.
The crew responsible for the build and giving it this name is German-based Thunderbike . That would be a group of people with such a passion for the American-made motorcycles that they've literally created hundreds of builds based on them.
With such a large portfolio under their name, the Thunderbike people have pretty much gone through all the possible custom styles. Chicanos, naturally, are properly represented.
We've covered quite a lot of these builds here on autoevolution, but I have to say, so far I haven't seen anything as extreme as El Sicario. Maybe it's the color scheme chosen for it, or the flamboyant bodywork it wears, or maybe something else, but that's the way it makes me feel.
It's unclear what model year the Heritage it is based on was born into, but that matters little in the grand scheme of things. What matters is the fact that the bike is so heavily modified that it instantly captures the attention.
It wears wheels much larger than they originally were, sized 23 inches at the front and 18 inches at the rear – the proper dimensions for a build of this kind. The huge wheel at the front also displays a massive, 340 mm brake disc, accompanied by fresh calipers.
Above each wheel, Thunderbike fitted massive fenders, sculpted in such a way as to visually stretch the two-wheeler and make it pop out. Up on the frame, a special seat made of cowhide and crocodile skin can be seen.
The way the bike feels to the rider has changed a lot compared to the base motorcycle . At the front, the fork, now packing an air ride system, comes with an extra six degrees of rake, achieved by fitting a dedicated triple tree, and a 14-inch (35 cm) handlebar fitted on old-school risers is what allows control.
At the rear, it too supported by an air-ride suspension, there is a custom swingarm kit, and the brake disc, usually fitted on the right side, has been moved to the left, which is also where the license plate has been moved.
Other minor touches do wonders in modifying the look of El Sicario, including the custom headlight fairing, the lights, the mirrors, and the several covers that dress the design in key places.
Thunderbike left the bike's stock Softail frame and its Milwaukee-Eight engine in their factory configuration, but even those might seem modified when drowned in so many custom modifications.
When everything was said and done, Thunderbike went for a bright green color for the body, adorned with special pinstriping. The effect is, as you can see, simply mesmerizing.
The German crew spent around $16,000 on the parts that went into the build alone, and that shows. Sadly, we have no info on how much was spent on the paint job and the man-hours invested in this.

Kuehne + Nagel attributed most of its third-quarter airfreight growth to market share gains, and expects to keep winning business into 2027 as a strong peak season gets under way.
Airfreight volumes rose 10% year on year, with chief executive Stefan Paul estimating underlying market growth at 3-4% and attributing 60-70% of K+N’s growth to market share gains.
“[It’s] pretty much coming from hard cargo. Hard cargo had a double-digit increase in terms of volume this quarter, and ecommerce went down significantly,” he told analysts yesterday.
Asked whether further market share gains would follow next year, he replied: “Similar to this year, it should continue.”
Separate analysis from Aevean illustrates the weakening backdrop for Chinese low-value ecommerce air exports. Tonnage fell 19% year on year in September, taking the decline over the first nine months to 4%.
Low-value ecommerce volumes to Europe halved in September, while those to North America were down 4%.
Technology has also replaced business lost from the automotive sector, revealing a longer-term shift in the forwarder’s airfreight customer base.
Mr Paul recalled that, five to seven years ago, K+N had a strong automotive business out of Europe, serving major manufacturers and their first- and second-tier suppliers. That business had been replaced by technology cargo, he said.
“I wouldn’t say we have an overdependency now on this, but it has replaced the shrinking auto sector on a one-to-one basis.”
Management declined to quantify its technology exposure or specify the contribution of hyperscaler customers to growth. However, chief financial officer Markus Blanka-Graff confirmed that “the hyperscaler is a good part of our growth in 2026”.
“I think our view currently is that growth in that space, with the customers we continuously gain, is also going to continue into 2027,” he added.
Mr Paul said half of K+N’s airfreight capacity came from its own charter operations, with the remainder covered by block space agreements. Improving the cargo mix, with a focus on hard cargo, would remain a priority into next year, he added.
Mr Blanka-Graff explained: “The stronger profitability, the stronger margins are on the hard cargo side and special products, healthcare side, hi-tech side.”

After Nearly 7 Years, Tesla Confirms the Cybertruck Isn't Coming to Australia
11 photos
Photo: Tesla / edited
Not surprising anyone, Tesla has ended its Cybertruck plans for Australia and New Zealand. This development leaves reservation holders with their money back, plus a shameful pitch for completely different Tesla models. The one-year FSD subscription in the cancellation email applies only when a customer orders a new Model 3 or Model Y, and this complimentary subscription is anything but compensation for nearly 7 years of waiting.
Tesla will send a separate email asking reservation holders to confirm their refund details, then process the payment within 30 days of confirmation. As if almost 7 years of waiting wasn't enough. Reservations opened in 2019, when the Cybertruck was both all the rage and the most ridiculed production vehicle of all time. Australian customers had to put down AUD 150 deposits, and the reservation scheme curiously outlived the Australian order page.
The American electric vehicle automaker closed it back in 2022, and even more curiously, Tesla did not automatically return everybody's deposits. With this email, Tesla is finally giving those would-be customers a definitive answer. Why didn't the company end things in 2024? As it happens, a publicity tour briefly revived hopes of a right-hand-drive version for this part of the world.
Someone at Tesla even decided on shipping a Cybertruck to Australia, displaying it at public events and in showrooms around the country to (re)build hype. Showing the Cybertruck to potential customers isn't the same as preparing a right-hand-drive model with the definitive plan of selling the Cybertruck in Australia.
That's not all, though, because Teslas for Australia and New Zealand require fine-tuning suited for said countries. Developing this variant makes little financial sense, and Elon Musk argued that himself during the 2024 shareholder meeting. Worse still, the commercial picture has also changed since the Cybertruck's way too pompous unveiling.
Photo: Tesla Instead of selling 250,000 units per annum, with possibilities of higher volumes, the Cybertruck barely moved 21,000 units in the United States of America last year. In the first three quarters of 2026, fewer than 12,000 units were delivered. Given that American drivers aren't particularly convinced either, why should Tesla pour valuable R&D money into developing and certifying a low-volume Cybertruck version for Australia and New Zealand?
The Full Self-Driving (Supervised) offer in the email is best viewed as a slap in the face to the peeps who gave the Cybertruck a chance in the first place. With FSD retailing at AUD 149 per month, a full year would be AUD 1,788, which is not nearly enough for wasting one's time like this.
While said offer may be useful to someone who already plans to buy the Model 3 or Y, it feels like rubbing salt in the wound of reservation holders who wanted the pickup and nothing else. Otherwise put, a coupon for a purchase they never intended to make rather than cash compensation.
As of this writing, the Cybertruck carries a starting price of USD 74,990 stateside, making it way pricier than a combustion half-ton pickup with four-wheel drive. Opting for the Premium grade means $84,990 from the outset, whereas $99,990 gets you the performance-oriented Cyberbeast.
Both the base Dual Motor All-Wheel Drive and the Premium All-Wheel Drive top 325 miles (523 kilometers) on a full charge. As for acceleration, Tesla says the Cyberbeast needs only 2.6 clicks to hit 60 mph (97 kph).

By Nils Roche
23 October 2026
Two sets of numbers have landed in the same week.
On 19 October, data from Norway’s Centre for High North Logistics (CHNL) showed 104 ships had crossed Russia’s Northern Sea Route (NSR) by 30 September, already more than in all of 2025.
Four days earlier, Lloyd’s List Intelligence reported that containerships moved 2.19m teu through the Suez Canal last month, the most since the Houthi campaign began, and Linerlytica expects carriers to be fully back to Suez by the first quarter of 2027.
Most coverage reads the first as proof that the Arctic is finally opening, but read together, they say something else: the part of the NSR Moscow planned and paid for has missed its targets by a wide margin, while the part it barely planned for has beaten them, because other people’s chokepoints closed.
Next summer will be the first test of what that growth is worth once they reopen.
A plan that fell short
In May 2018, Vladimir Putin set a target of 80m tonnes of NSR cargo a year by 2024. A 2022 development plan, costed at about RUB1.8trn ($29.7bn), kept that goal and added 150m tonnes for 2030. The route carried 37.9m tonnes in 2024 and 37m tonnes in 2025, its first fall since 2022. Rosatom expects about 40m tonnes this year – half the 2024 target, two years late.
Almost all of it is Russian cargo from Russian ports, mainly Yamal LNG (21.3m tonnes in 2025) and crude from the Ob Gulf and Pechora Sea (7.8m tonnes). Growth was meant to come from Arctic LNG 2 and Rosneft’s Vostok Oil. Sanctions crippled the first; the second is years behind.
Source: CHNL
The “Polar Silk Road” did not make it into the outline of the 15th Five-Year Plan, approved on 12 March this year. It isn’t that the NSR is missing from an Arctic section; the Arctic silk road itself is absent.
Even the 14th Five-Year Plan (2021–25), which did include the concept, stated only the aim to “take part in practical Arctic cooperation and build the Ice Silk Road”. The route was always implied, not named.
The transit surprise
Transit cargo, the part foreign shippers care about, tells the opposite story. Russian officials once projected 1m tonnes in 2024 and 2m tonnes in 2030. CHNL estimates 3.7m tonnes was actually carried in the first nine months of 2026 alone.
Look inside it: 22 tankers carried about 2.1m tonnes of crude east from Murmansk, Primorsk, and Ust-Luga. In 2024, 95% of transit cargo went from Russia to China. This is less an Asia–Europe shortcut than a sanctions-era export lane that avoids Baltic inspections, Black Sea drones, and the Red Sea.
Containers a footnote
By 30 September, CHNL counted four voyages linking Asia and Europe, with no Russian port at either end. Sea Legend’s China–Europe Arctic Express completed eight sailings on seven ships of 1,500 to 4,900 teu, the last two leaving China early, on 27 September, because ice was forecast. Ningbo Customs says they carried 7,761 teu; other reports claim more than 14,000 teu, against about 15,700 teu offered.
Whatever the final figure, it is clear the season moved less than one 24,000 teu ship carries on a single Suez sailing.
Source: CHNL
Physical limits unchanged
About 12.5 metres of draught in the Sannikov Strait caps containerships at roughly 5,000 teu, while ships without high ice-class have a three-month window, in a good year. Every voyage needs a permit from Rosatom’s NSR Administration, which also sets the route and the escort.
I costed the loop the way a carrier’s network team would: a 4,900 teu ship, eight seasonal sailings, west through the Arctic and back via Suez. At October charter and bunker prices and half-full ships, a slot costs about twice a Suez slot, despite a shorter distance of 2,200 nautical miles. Per slot per day, a 4,900 teu ship costs nearly three times as much to charter as a 24,000 teu vessel.
The escort adds $150,000-$280,000 a transit, and Chinese sources put Arctic hull and P&I cover at three to five times normal rates. If the higher volume claim is right and the ships sailed nearly full, the gap narrows, but does not close. The carbon case fails too: small, part-loaded ships at 18 knots emit more CO₂ per box than a Suez ULCV.
Shippers paying that premium are buying neither speed nor lower emissions. They are buying a corridor the Houthis, Iran, and the US Navy cannot close. Only Russia can, since it issues the permits and runs the icebreakers.
Who pays?
The price is low because Moscow keeps it low. Escort tariffs were capped in roubles in 2014, so their dollar value has more than halved, and about half of the icebreaker programme is funded from the federal budget. The Far East ministry says escorting one ship now costs about RUB60m, against RUB16m a decade ago. A new tariff order is in draft, and in September the transport ministry proposed a per-tonne levy on Russian exporters to fund two more icebreakers.
The bill is being moved around; it has not gone away. The delivery schedule of 120MW Rossiya – a nuclear-powered tug, and flagship of the year-round promise which is expected to be break ice up to four metres thick and create a 50-metre wide channel – has slipped from 2027 to the end of 2029.
Western carriers will not fill the gap. Atomflot has been under US sanctions since 2023, and MSC, CMA CGM, and Hapag-Lloyd have pledged not to use Arctic routes. Cosco has stayed out since 2022, leaving the risk to private operators such as Sea Legend and NewNew Shipping.
The case for patience
The strongest counter-argument is that ice is retreating, Beijing is patient and transit has beaten every forecast, so the planners may have been wrong only about timing.
I am not convinced. Transit grew in exactly the years the Red Sea was shut, Hormuz was fought over, and Russia’s westbound exports were blocked. Those are shocks, not trends. With Hormuz still contested, the eastbound crude may hold up for a while. The battery and EV boxes are another matter. Once Asia–North Europe strings are back on weekly Suez rotations with 24,000 teu ships, a Chinese exporter will be offered a cheaper, year-round, sanctions-free alternative.
Next season will tell us: whether Sea Legend can fill its NSR ships with Suez in use; what Russia’s new tariff will cost for foreign transits; and whether Cosco comes back, which would mean Beijing judges the sanctions-risk worth taking.
Until then, the NSR is not a tradelane . It is an insurance policy that Russia writes and Russia underwrites, and which China buys only when the other routes are on fire.

Aerial view of Queensway gold project in Newfoundland and Labrador. Credit: New Found Gold.
Posted By: Colin McClelland October 23, 2026
New Found Gold (TSX, NYSE-A: NFGC) has more than doubled the projected value of its Queensway gold project in Newfoundland to C$1.73 billion while expanding measured and indicated resources by 38%, according to a revised preliminary economic assessment (PEA).
Last year’s study estimated an after-tax net present value of C$743 million at a 5% discount rate. The revised PEA assumes a gold price of $3,600 per oz., 44% above the earlier $2,500 assumption, while estimating initial capital costs at C$150 million, the company said Thursday in a release.
“Our flagship Queensway asset is uniquely attractive, with a high-grade core that starts at surface. It is located in central Newfoundland, close to infrastructure and a skilled workforce,” CEO Keith Boyle said in the release.
Queensway would give New Found a much larger production base than its recently commissioned Hammerdown mine, with projected average output of 116,000 oz. annually over 15 years. The company says the initial stage is fully funded and expects cash generated from mining to pay for later expansion, although permits and further development work remain.
Shares in New Found gained 3% to C$2.27 apiece on Friday morning in Toronto, for a market capitalization of C$872.4 million. The stock has traded in a 12-month range of C$1.88 to C$4.89.
Larger resource
Measured and indicated resources total 27.3 million tonnes grading 2.19 grams gold per tonne for 1.92 million oz., including a contribution from the new Dropkick zone. Inferred resources total 12.5 million tonnes grading 1.51 grams gold for 606,000 ounces. The estimate is effective July 6.
The revised mine plan would produce 1.74 million oz. of gold, with annual output peaking at 190,000 oz. in 2032. It projects an after-tax internal rate of return of 126%, payback in less than a year and all-in sustaining costs of $1,375 an ounce. First processing is targeted for late 2027.
The earlier study projected about 1.5 million oz. over the same mine life, a 56.3% return and all-in sustaining costs of $1,256 an ounce. The higher gold-price assumption prevents a direct comparison of the two studies’ headline valuations.
Plant changes
The revised plan sends initial feed from the Keats and Iceberg open pits to New Found’s Pine Cove plant, replacing the earlier proposal to use Nugget Pond. Pine Cove is being converted to a gravity and carbon-in-leach circuit, with expansion to 1,400 tonnes a day planned. Queensway would initially supply 700 tonnes a day, averaging 13.41 grams gold.
Underground mining would begin in 2030, earlier in the development sequence than previously planned. The revised plan increases underground gold ounces by 86%, partly to reduce waste stripping and partly because of a high-grade shoot identified at Dropkick.
A new plant at Queensway would begin operating in 2031 at 4,900 tonnes a day, ending shipments to Pine Cove. Separate circuits would process higher-grade feed and lower-grade or refractory material. A subsequent expansion would lift total capacity to 7,000 tonnes a day.
Beyond the C$149.8-million initial investment, the study includes C$832.1 million in growth capital and C$970.8 million in sustaining capital. New Found expects operating cash flow to fund the later stages at the study’s assumed gold price.
The company held about C$167 million in cash at Sept. 30 against C$70 million in debt. A further C$35-million debt facility is available subject to conditions.
Queensway still requires environmental clearance and subsequent permits. The current environmental assessment covers the Keats, Iceberg, Dome and Jackpot open pits; later deposits, underground development and processing expansions would require their own regulatory approvals.
Hammerdown ramps up
At Hammerdown, which reached commercial production on Aug. 19 , third-quarter output totalled 4,863 oz., bringing year-to-date production to 10,670 oz., New Found said in its Oct. 15 operating update . Full third-quarter financial results are scheduled for Nov. 11.
Quarterly production fell 13% short of SCP Resource Finance’s estimate, mainly because processed grades were lower than expected as crusher and sorter commissioning shifted into early 2027. Even so, year-to-date output exceeded its forecast by 5%, while mining and processing volumes were ahead of expectations, SCP analyst Eleanor Magdzinski said in an Oct. 15 note.
“We view today’s first quarterly results as positive, with YTD26 gold production of 10,670 oz (+5% vs SCPe) and mining activity materially ahead of expectations, highlighting a strong ramp-up,” Magdzinski said.
The firm maintained its buy rating and C$5 share-price target. Its assessment preceded the revised Queensway study.
New Found expects Hammerdown to produce at an annual rate of 20,000 to 25,000 oz. over its mine life at all-in sustaining costs of about $2,500 per ounce. The crusher and sorter are intended to lower crushing costs and improve grades delivered to Pine Cove.
“More importantly for investors, in under a year, New Found Gold has built a successful operations team in central Newfoundland,” Boyle said in the production release. “We will now use the knowledge and experience gained from bringing Hammerdown into production and focus on advancing our fully funded flagship Queensway Gold Project to production.”

New York City Has a Taste for Luxury, and the Name on Everyone's Lips Is the 2026 Lexus RX
14 photos
Photo: Eli Khalifa & SOS Auto Group/Facebook
New York City is arguably the worst place in America to own a car. Although it really depends on which borough you call home. If you’re in “the city”, meaning Manhattan, then you’re way better off using public transportation, as the vast majority of Manhattanites do. Besides, the cost of parking is on par with the GDP of a small African nation. Wakanda.
Yet, New Yorkers still buy cars, and expensive ones too. According to a report published by CarEdge , the most popular new vehicle in NYC for the past 45 days is the 2026 Lexus RX. And by most popular, I mean the best-selling car – 137 units sold over that time period.
To me, this comes as a surprise. Usually, it’ll be something like the Toyota RAV4, Honda CR-V or the Corolla. Not a Lexus. But as we’ve come to learn, the Japanese premium carmaker has magical powers when it comes to the U.S. market. You just utter the word Lexus and people think reliability, quality and resale value, the likes of which you’re not going to get with any of its German rivals.
I don’t necessarily agree, but perception is reality. This is as true in life as it is in the automotive industry.
Over the same 45-day period, the Lexus NX came fourth with 62 units sold, while the larger Lexus TX rounded out the top 5 with 54 units. That’s three Lexus models in the top 5, plus a Mercedes-Benz (GLE) at no.3.
To be fair, before we crown the RX the king of New York City , there’s an important distinction to be made here. CarEdge only looked at sales activity at dealerships associated with a particular location, and not all purchases made by NYC residents period. This is not a census of every vehicle sold to residents across all five boroughs.
Does this make the results any less intriguing? No way, Jose. I mean Johnny!
Five boroughs, Five New Yorks Manhattan is the home of the yellow cab, the Empire State Building, Chrysler Building, Central Park, and Madison Square Garden. Implicitly it’s the home of the New York Knicks and the New York Rangers. Brooklyn, on the other hand, is a proper cultural melting pot. A sort of mix between the Upper West Side of Manhattan and Queens. It’s also the home of the Brooklyn Nets. Nobody likes them.
Speaking of Queens, I think this might just be the most fascinating of the five boroughs for reasons I won’t go into right now. It’s the home of the New York Mets. Everyone likes them.
The Bronx? That’s where the Bombers live – aka the New York Yankees . As for Staten Island, it’s sort of a mix between NYC and New Jersey. By the way, the NFL’s NY Giants and Jets play across the Hudson river in New Jersey at Metlife Stadium, so they’re technically not in NYC.
Photo: Lexus Anyway, the point is that all five boroughs are different and the fact that different types of cars can be found topping borough-specific rankings makes perfect sense. For instance, Brooklyn’s best-selling new car in the aforementioned period? The 2026-27 Honda CR-V. In Queens? The 2026 Subaru Forester.
But it’s the Lexus RX that seems to occupy this particularly interesting middle ground. This is a premium SUV, or luxury SUV as some call it – although I wish people would stop saying that. Brands such as Mercedes, BMW, Audi and Lexus are not luxury brands. Rolls-Royce and Bentley are luxury brands. It’s pretty easy to make that distinction.
Long Island City: home of the Lexus RX This is where the most RX sales took place and that does make sense to me. Even though it’s technically a part of Queens, Long Island City has more in common with some of NYC’s more affluent neighborhoods as opposed to the suburban, Doug & Carrie, King of Queens-like image many Americans associate with Queens.
According to a report from the New York State Comptroller, Long Island City’s median household income was approximately $162,100 in 2023 – almost twice that of Sunnyside and Woodside.
But why the RX? Well, it’s large enough without being particularly cumbersome. It’s a proper mid-size SUV at 192.5 inches (4.9 m) in length, but you can maneuver it around way more easily than you would an Escalade or Navigator. And yet it still provides enough luggage space for a weekend getaway to the Hamptons (just watch out for ugly babies), to go with versatile powertrain choices.
The best choice being the RX 350h, which combines a naturally aspirated gasoline engine with an electric motor. This variant doesn’t require you to plug the car in, which is a major advantage in a city where having access to a dedicated parking space is already considered a major privilege – let alone one equipped with an EV charger.
Photo: Lexus Yes, a PHEV or BEV would be fantastic for someone with a wall charger at home. But if you often rely on commercial parking garages and/or street parking, the conventional hybrid is the way to go.
It’s also possible that New York City might not even “want” to own what some might consider the best luxury car. They might simply want the least complicated one. And this is true in Beverly Hills as well, another location where the Lexus RX recently came out on top, sales-wise. The RX; not the Range Rover , or the Cayenne or the Escalade.
How much is the RX? While the 2027 model year variant is already out, the 2026 RX is still for sale and the absolute cheapest one you can get is the RX 350 from $52,775. That’s the gasoline-powered front wheel drive variant. Meanwhile, the RX 350h AWD (the hybrid) starts from $55,075. Whether you think that’s a lot or a little, is entirely up to you.
All I’ll say is that the all-new 2027 BMW X5 starts from $72,110.

Tesla’s proposed $10 billion “Project Crystal Sun” solar factory in Texas could get up to 35 years of local tax breaks on its equipment, according to the four agreements Fort Bend County commissioners approved on Thursday.
The vote was 4-0. And Tesla still hasn’t committed to building the plant in Texas.
From a tax filing to four agreements
As we first reported in August , Tesla applied for a 10-year school property tax limitation under the state’s JETI program, through Lamar CISD and the Texas Comptroller. The plan is a vertically integrated solar plant near Richmond, southwest of Houston, that would make everything from silicon ingots to finished modules, with commercial production targeted for Q1 2029.
Lamar CISD approved the school tax piece in September. The county was next.
Advertisement - scroll for more content
On October 22, the commissioners court approved items 25A to 25D on its agenda: a Chapter 312 tax abatement , a Chapter 381 incentive agreement , a foreign trade zone agreement with a payment in lieu of taxes (PILOT), and a “true up” PILOT agreement . Interim County Judge Daniel Wong abstained because his engineering firm has worked with Tesla.
Each agreement covers a different slice of Tesla’s tax bill, and together they run for decades.
Years 1 to 10: no county tax on equipment or inventory
The Chapter 312 agreement abates 100% of county property taxes on Tesla’s equipment and other tangible personal property at the plant for 10 tax years. The clock starts in tax year 2029 by default, but Tesla can move it to the first year after production starts, as late as 2031 without needing the county’s approval.
Tesla’s JETI application splits the $10.1 billion into $1.52 billion of real property and $8.6 billion of personal property, mostly production equipment.
Land and buildings aren’t part of the deal. Anything that isn’t eligible for the abatement, including the land and buildings, stays “fully taxable at all times,” according to the agreement.
Inventory goes through the foreign trade zone deal instead. Tesla’s site would be part of Port Freeport’s Foreign-Trade Zone No. 149, which exempts eligible inventory from local property tax. In exchange for the county not objecting, Tesla agreed to make PILOT payments, set at “zero dollars or 0%” of the forgone taxes for as long as the abatement is in effect.
Years 11 to 30: Tesla gets 90% back
When the abatement ends, the Chapter 381 agreement takes over. Tesla starts paying county taxes on its equipment, and the county pays 90% of them back as an annual grant for 20 years. The county keeps 10% for its general fund.
Inventory follows the same pattern. After the abatement, Tesla’s FTZ payment rises to 10% of the taxes that would otherwise apply.
The 12,000-job bonus
There’s one more lever. If Tesla averages at least 12,000 employees for any two consecutive years during the first decade, the first five years of the rebate period become a 100% grant, and the rebate period stretches from 20 to 25 years.
That pushes the agreement out to Project Year 35. It’s also 2,288 jobs above the 9,712 Tesla says it will create.
What Tesla has to deliver
To keep the tax breaks, Tesla has to start construction by June 30, 2027, begin “regular commercial production of solar cells” by December 31, 2030, and invest $10 billion by the later of December 31, 2031 or two years after production starts. Force majeure and “ERCOT Delay” provisions can extend those dates.
The jobs ramp is 2,500, 5,000, 7,500, then 9,712 employees by the fourth year of operations, with an average compensation of $55 per hour. Tesla gets the full abatement as long as it hits 90% of the headcount target, which is about 8,741 people.
The penalties are mild. Missing a jobs or wage target for one year only costs Tesla that year’s break, and two misses in a row lets the county terminate the agreement. Full recapture of abated taxes, plus a possible 15% penalty if they aren’t repaid within 60 days, is reserved for “Material Defaults” like missing the $10 billion investment, blowing the construction deadlines or abandoning the plant for 12 months.
Under the Chapter 381 deal, grants from earlier years can’t be clawed back for a headcount shortfall.
The county’s floor is small. The true-up agreement only guarantees that Fort Bend collects at least $2 million a year, and 25% of the taxes Tesla pays on its real property, the county’s 10% share and the FTZ payments all count toward that total.
For scale, Tesla’s own consultant, Kroll, estimated in the JETI filing that the project would pay $276.5 million in Fort Bend County general taxes over 38 years without incentives, peaking at $16.2 million in 2030. That estimate lumps land, buildings and equipment together. The equipment portion is the one the county just agreed to give back, for most of those years.
Shopping for the best deal
In its application, it says the economics of the Fort Bend site are “not competitive” with an unnamed site in another state without the JETI limitation and local abatements. The competing state is redacted in a confidential supplement.
None of the documents state a production capacity. The only big number is a quote from Elon Musk at Davos in January, cited in the application: “The SpaceX and Tesla team, both separately, are working to build to 100 GW a year of solar power in the U.S., of manufactured solar power.”
For comparison, Qcells is spending $2.5 billion on its ingot-to-module campus in Cartersville, Georgia, where a 3.5 GW cell line started production this year. Crystal Sun’s budget is four times that.
Tesla has been here before. New York spent $950 million on the Buffalo factory for Tesla’s solar business, and when the solar plans fell apart, Tesla turned to things other than solar to meet its employment requirements , including data labeling for Autopilot. Tesla did announce production of a new solar panel in Buffalo last year .
Electrek’s Take
We want this factory to happen. A US plant making its own ingots, wafers, cells and modules would be rare, and it’s one of the few parts of Tesla’s business that still lines up with the mission it used to talk about before its “awesome abundance” pivot based on AI.
But corporate America loves its tax breaks. For 10 years, Tesla pays no county tax on the $8.6 billion of equipment that makes up most of the project. For the next 20, it gets 90% of it back. In return, the county’s guaranteed minimum is $2 million a year, on a $10 billion plant. And Tesla still hasn’t said it’s coming.
That’s how site selection works now. Companies file, collect offers from several states, and the county that bids the most wins. Fort Bend’s economic development director, Carlos Guzman, told ABC13 the county “would’ve been eliminated from consideration” without these agreements. Hard to argue with that, and it’s exactly why these deals keep getting richer.

source_document.body:
Blue Bird plans to invest approximately $300 million in a school bus factory in Fort Valley, Georgia, creating 375 jobs over three years, according to an announcement from Gov. Brian Kemp.
What’s Related
The company will convert a former diesel-powered motorhome manufacturing site into a facility of about 1 million square feet. Construction is expected to begin in the first quarter of 2027.
The factory will produce Type C school buses, including diesel, gasoline, propane, and electric models. Planned hiring includes manufacturing, plant operations and technician positions.
The state announcement did not give an opening date, but Blue Bird’s May 2026 investor presentation identified the fourth quarter of 2028 as the anticipated production start for its new Fort Valley plant.
Factory plans include automation
Blue Bird’s earlier presentation described a factory designed to produce 9,000 Type C buses, with automation to begin when production starts. The company said separating products and adding automation would help improve manufacturing efficiency.
That presentation put the total investment at more than $300 million and identified $80 million in funding from the U.S. Department of Energy’s Office of Manufacturing and Energy Supply Chains. The October announcement did not update the status of that funding or disclose a dollar amount for state or local incentives.
The latest announcement places the project at an existing industrial property previously used to manufacture motorhomes. It also confirms that the planned school bus production will cover four fuel and power options, rather than electric buses alone.
Pride of Middle Georgia
Blue Bird already has more than 1,900 employees in Georgia, according to the state. The company expects to add 375 positions over three years, although the announcement did not break down hiring by year or job category.
“Every bus that rolls out of our plant carries the pride of the people across Middle Georgia who build it,” said John Wyskiel, Blue Bird’s president and CEO. The company directs applicants to its careers website for information about available positions.
The Georgia Department of Economic Development worked with the Development Authority of Peach County and Georgia Quick Start on the project. Fort Valley Mayor Shakeena B. Reeves pointed to the city’s longstanding relationship with the manufacturer.
“For generations, Fort Valley has helped Blue Bird move America forward,” Reeves said.

source_document.body:
Saudi Arabia appears to be expanding its ballistic missile factory to build larger solid-fuel missiles that could fly farther or carry heavier payloads, according to two U.S. researchers who analyzed more than a year of commercial satellite images.
More capable missiles could help Saudi Arabia to deter attacks by Iran and make its military more self-reliant, while possibly strengthening its position in a deadly conflict with Yemen’s Tehran-backed Houthi fighters.
But they risk fueling a regional missile race and could deepen opposition in the U.S. Congress to a U.S.-Saudi civilian nuclear agreement that has already raised concerns about proliferation.
Satellite company Planet Labs, based in the U.S., took images of the al-Duwadimi complex about 125 miles west of Riyadh between April 2025 and September 2026.
The two researchers, Sam Lair and Michael Duitsman of the Foreign Policy Research Institute, assessed that those images show a new building that houses casting pits — wells in which a mixture of fuel ingredients is poured into missile motor casings and allowed to harden.
The Saudi embassy and Information Ministry did not respond to requests for comment.
The building, flanked by what appear to be walls to protect nearby structures from accidental explosions, is at least twice as large as the one believed to house the plant’s existing casting pits, Lair and Duitsman said in their assessment. The Foreign Policy Research Institute (FPRI) is a non-partisan research organization in Philadelphia.
A second new building could be used to store fuel ingredients or finished missile components, they said.
The imagery “suggests that Saudi Arabia is expanding the infrastructure at the missile production complex, likely to produce larger missiles which could deliver larger payloads or reach longer ranges,” they wrote.
Militaries favor solid-fuel missiles because they can be stored for long periods and launched more quickly than liquid-fuel systems.
Lair and Duitsman and experts from the London-based International Institute for Strategic Studies (IISS) and the CNA research and analysis organization told Reuters that the makeup of Saudi Arabia’s missile force suggests that the al-Duwadimi complex relies on Chinese technology. Lair and Duitsman said that its characteristics are also similar to Chinese missile plants.
Saudi Arabia secretly acquired about 40 liquid-fuel DF-3 ballistic missiles from China in 1987, according to a 1991 declassified CIA estimate. It displayed two of them for the first time in an April 2014 military parade, according to a YouTube video and photographs of the event.
The FPRI team also recently identified from social media videos and photos what they assessed was the wreckage in Yemen of a Saudi-fired Chinese-designed DF-15 missile.
Lair said the kingdom may now be producing the solid-fuel DF-15, and that the expansion of a1-Dumadimi is likely for the production of the longer-range DF-21 or a similar missile.
Riyadh is believed to have turned to Beijing because Washington has long restricted exports of longer-range missile systems.
The Chinese embassy and defense ministry did not respond to requests for comment. The CIA declined to comment. The White House did not respond to a request for comment.
Missiles would alter the balance of power
Sascha Bruchmann, a research fellow at IISS, said longer-range missiles would allow Saudi Arabia to strike Iran without risking its U.S.-supplied F-15 jet fighters against Iranian air defenses.
“You’d want a system to threaten whatever is holy to Tehran ... if you don’t have the political will to send an F-15 with JDAMs over Tehran,” said Bruchmann, referring to U.S.-made satellite-guided bombs. “Iran has a lead because its missiles and drones can strike Saudi wherever it wants. The Saudis could close that capability gap a bit.”
Bruchmann, who reviewed the FPRI analysis at Reuters request, concurred that the expansion of al-Duwadimi could be for producing more powerful solid-fuel missiles.
Janes, the defense intelligence company, also reviewed it and said the buildings “may suggest an effort to expand production capability or support the development of longer-range missiles.”
Saudi Arabia’s apparent pursuit of more powerful missiles comes as other Gulf powers are also seeking to expand their offensive and defensive arsenals, said Decker Eveleth, a CNA analyst who has been tracking the al-Duwadimi construction with commercial satellite imagery and concurred with the FPRI assessment.
“This is being replicated across the Middle East,” he said. “You see exactly the same thing happening in the UAE. You see the exact same thing happening in Turkey. Everybody is doing this now.”
The expansion of al-Duwadimi could have political consequences in the US by stiffening bipartisan congressional opposition to a US-Saudi agreement under which the US would help Riyadh establish uranium enrichment for power generation.
Opponents say that the deal lacks sufficient safeguards to prevent Riyadh from secretly building a nuclear weapon. The kingdom has denied any such plan.
Work began last year
The FPRI assessment said the Planet Labs imagery showed that the expansion at al-Duwadimi began in April 2025 with ground-clearing and digging for the suspected storage building. Work on the suspected casting-pit building began later that month or in early May, it said.
A December 12, 2025, photo showed what researchers assessed were two deep pits inside the building that had no roof yet.
A Sept. 18, 2026, photo shows the roof still partly missing and “heavy duty blast diverting walls” on either side to prevent accidental explosions from damaging adjacent structures.
The walls, the researchers said, are somewhat similar to those depicted in imagery of US and Iranian missile plants and “further evidence the building is for casting solid propellant motors.”
Finishing the roofs would not take long, the FPRI said, but installing casting equipment may take several months. The facility could be ready to start producing missiles as early as the end of the year.

source_document.body:
Freight technology vendors are selling AI agents that can benchmark rates and award freight under rules a customer sets. A new survey finds most supply chain organizations still limit AI to generating insights, and the first obstacle the research names is their own workforce.
The Association for Supply Chain Management (ASCM) and the Digital Supply Chain Institute (DSCI) released The People Paradox in Supply Chain AI Integration on Oct. 14. Of the supply chain professionals surveyed, 83% said their employees are unprepared to use AI effectively. The 17% who described their workforce as ready reported a 71% AI project success rate. Everyone else reported 28%, and about 64% of that group is still in the pilot or planning stage.
Abe Eshkenazi, CEO of ASCM, said most AI sessions at supply chain conferences run through the same agenda: the challenges, the implementation, and the benefits. Every one of them ends with a reminder not to forget about the people, he said.
“It’s interesting because from our perspective that’s where you ought to start the conversation,” Eshkenazi told FreightWaves.
AI mostly stays in planning
The report scored AI adoption across 13 core supply chain functions on a scale from 1, meaning no AI use, to 5, meaning autonomous execution without human review. The average was 1.94.
Planning functions scored highest, led by demand planning at 2.28 and supply and inventory planning at 2.12. Execution-heavy functions trailed, and returns and reverse logistics ranked last at 1.59.
The report calls this keeping AI on a “short leash” and says companies doing it are using predictive tools as “little more than digital spreadsheets.” Eshkenazi reached for the same image.
“I think we’re using it much more on the analysis and on the predictions as opposed to the doing,” he said, calling it “more of a glorified spreadsheet.”
He sees room for AI to take on “routine transactional decisions where AI can operate within parameters,” with people keeping the higher-risk calls on customer commitments, sourcing, and major disruptions.
“We need to expand the AI authority, but we need to do so with confidence in the technology, and it’s not there right now,” he said.
Skills and ROI top the barriers
Two barriers tied for the top spot at 33% each: a lack of workforce skills and resources, and an unclear business case or return on investment. Poor data quality followed at 25%. Executive skepticism did not make the list of main hurdles.
Eshkenazi compared AI to enterprise resource planning (ERP) systems, which were also expected to revolutionize supply chains.
“The technology solution can’t improve bad process and it can’t improve bad data,” he said.
Companies should use value stream mapping and data analysis to find and fix problem areas before an ERP project starts, he said.
Headcount reduction is too simple a measure of AI’s return, in his view. The better one is response time: how quickly a company can recognize a disruption, weigh alternatives, and act.
“You can’t point to a system and say it made the decision,” Eshkenazi said. “Ultimately, somebody has to own that decision for the organization.”
Involvement drops below the C-suite
The survey found that 82% of C-suite respondents lead, implement, or scale AI initiatives. At the director level, 12% lead AI efforts directly, and half of directors said they are only aware of them. The aware-only share rises to 51% of managers and 70% of staff.
Those breakdowns rest on small samples. The survey collected 144 responses, and 107 met the criteria for analysis. Only 11 respondents were C-suite executives, and the report labels its results by job level as directional.
Few expect AI to replace workers
Only 7% of respondents predict AI will directly replace workers, while 51% expect it to move people toward higher-value decision-making.
Eshkenazi said that shift carries a cost. Supply chain professionals used to build judgment by running the analysis, building the reports, and working the spreadsheets, which taught them to spot exceptions and ask whether the numbers looked right.
“A lot of those foundational activities and experiences are now being taken over by AI, and we’re moving individuals into positions where they have to make decisions and manage without understanding the fundamentals,” he said.
Technology more powerful than companies are using, paired with workers who can’t critically think through what it produces, is “a very dangerous combination for organizations,” he said.
Cyber concerns outpace safeguards
Of those surveyed, 92% expressed significant concern about cybersecurity exposure through AI-enabled suppliers and trade partners. According to the report, the average organization had adopted 2.3 of six standard cybersecurity practices.
Eshkenazi traced the exposure to the visibility push that followed the pandemic, when companies began connecting suppliers, carriers, and brokers on shared platforms.
“It’s exposing them to significant ransomware and cybersecurity risks in their tier-three and their tier-four vendors, where predominantly they don’t have a lot of resources,” he said.
Food distributors on a conference panel in San Antonio described one way that plays out: a compromised carrier email that led to a fraudulent pickup of a cold-storage load .
Calling a tier-four vendor for inventory and delivery status isn’t an option, he said. “Huge opportunity but also significant risk,” he said.
Start with one process
Eshkenazi’s first recommendation is to pick one high-value process, such as a key customer process, supplier, or route, and involve the people who run it.
“Then establish measurable outcomes,” he said. “First, you have to identify where you’re starting from.”
That work has to reach below the leadership level, he said, so employees see AI as a path to more valuable work.
“Just because it’s a technology solution doesn’t make it autonomous and doesn’t make it better if you don’t have qualified processes, if you don’t have knowledgeable workers, and if you don’t have clean data,” Eshkenazi said.
Why it matters: Vendors are selling AI that can act on freight decisions, but most supply chain organizations still use it for analysis. The ASCM and DSCI survey ties that caution to unready workers, unclear returns, and thin cybersecurity safeguards.

You Can Now Request a Curbside EV Charger Near Your Home if You Live in Seattle
6 photos
Photo: Seattle City Light
Owning an EV is not very practical if you live in an apartment building and don't have the option to install a charger at home. Seattle is a special case, with more than half of homes being apartments and condos. The city wants to make it easier for EV owners to charge their EVs by installing up to 200 public curbside chargers.
Owning an electric vehicle might not be the same for everyone. Ideally, an EV owner would have a garage or alley where they can charge their vehicle at the lowest electricity rates possible. Having solar power makes this situation even better. However, for many EV owners in big cities, charging at home is not always an option. This changes the economics entirely, as public charging may be expensive, difficult to access, or both.
Those living in apartment buildings in a big city are especially affected, as they probably park their cars on the street. They don't have the possibility of installing a charger unless local administration takes this possibility into account. Luckily for Seattle residents, the city is planning to install public curbside chargers in neighborhoods with limited charging options.
The program involves Seattle City Light and the Seattle Department of Transportation, and the plan is to install up to 200 Level-2 curbside EV chargers until 2030. Until fall 2027, residents can submit applications for new locations where they need public chargers installed. Based on their input, the two companies will select the best locations to install the chargers. City officials say that locations will be chosen in small batches on an ongoing basis.
While these chargers are intended to top up the battery while the car is parked near home, they might not be appropriate for overnight charging. The tariff is $0.21 per kWh, which is pretty close to the DC fast charging tariff that Seattle City Light charges, of $0.22 during off-peak hours ($0.36 on-peak). However, the convenience of having a curbside charger near home is priceless.
The expansion follows a pilot that the Seattle Department of Transportation ran at 31 locations in 2023 and 2024. The 58 chargers installed then were used intensively, and community feedback was positive, which is why the city decided to expand it next year. The new installations will be funded by the $1.55 billion transportation levy that voters already approved in 2024.
Installing the chargers should take about two weeks of work per location, with installations expected to start in fall 2027. Designing the sites and permitting will begin earlier, in spring 2027. The project will prioritize areas near multifamily houses that aren't currently served by curbside chargers. They will also favor sites near businesses and parks, which usually lead to higher utilization rates.

Photo: © Gary Blakeley | Dreamstime.com
By Charlotte Goldstone
23 October 2026
Containership charter rates have climbed to their highest level in four years, despite falling fixtures, and a record orderbook pointing to a major influx of capacity in 2028.
Braemar’s charter index is at 325.8, up 21% year on year and its highest level since autumn 2022. Meanwhile, the number of fixtures between 1 January and 17 October was down 15% year on year, at 853, while capacity fixed declined 10%, to 2.54m teu.
“A few weeks back we showed a record orderbook and a 2028 delivery wave the size of the 2002 fleet. You would expect charterers to be sitting back and waiting. They are not,” says today’s report.
The martime consultancy said the apparent contradiction reflected a shortage of prompt tonnage, with owners having secured long-term employment for vessels during 2024 and 2025.
Charterers are responding by booking further ahead, added Braemar, noting that on a capacity-weighted basis, ships are now being fixed an average of 7.8 months before delivery, against 6.8 months a year earlier. For vessels of 3,000 teu and above, the lead time exceeds 10 months.
In the third quarter, half of fixtures were for ships delivering more than three months ahead, compared with 23% across the same period of 2025.
At the same time, charter costs have diverged sharply from freight rates. While the Freightos Baltic Index (FBX) fell 61% between January and October 2025, Braemar’s charter index rose 3%.
“Relative to freight rates, charter costs have run at roughly double their 2021-2024 average,” Braemar highlighted.
The pressure is particularly evident in the feeder and panamax segments, vessels of 1,500-1,900 teu fixed for nine to 15 months now commanding a median $28,625 a day, up 18% year on year. Recent 12-month fixtures have even reached $36,500 a day, according to Braemar data.
In the 4,000-5,099 teu segment, fixtures fell 39%, while short-period rates rose to a median $58,000 a day, from $51,000.
Ships aged 20 years or more accounted for 30% of fixtures this year, up from 26% in 2025. A 20-year-old 1,700 teu feeder still earns a median $24,000 a day, while a panamax built in 1997 fixed at $50,000 a day in September.
Maersk has emerged as the busiest charterer, increasing fixtures by 14% and chartered capacity by 20%, despite the overall market contraction. CMA CGM, last year’s leading charterer, cut its fixtures by 41%.
However, the longer-term outlook is arguably less favourable for owners, warned Braemar analyst Jonathan Roach.
He highlighted that since January 2025, 94 fixtures, representing about 570,000 teu, had involved newbuildings scheduled for delivery in 2028. The largest delivery wave on record, paired with potential easing of Red Sea disruption and forecasted weaker demand in 2027, could all undermine charter rates.
“Charterers are queuing today. By 2028, owners may be the ones in the queue,” summerised Mr Roach.
